title: I’ve been working on Age of New Worlds, a turn-based 4X strategy game with hex maps
author: ernestwisniewski
selftext:
* An experimental browser version: [https://demo.aonw.net/](https://demo.aonw.net/)
* Windows/macOS/Android builds: [https://ernest-dev.itch.io/aonw](https://ernest-dev.itch.io/aonw)
* Devlog: [https://ernest.dev](https://ernest.dev)
* Github: [https://github.com/ernestwisniewski/aonw](https://github.com/ernestwisniewski/aonw)

AoNW is a hobby project. I’m developing it in my spare time, mostly as a way to experiment, learn new technologies, and build the kind of strategy game I personally enjoy.

LMs is part of the workflow, but I'm trying to use it more as a tool for iteration than as a "generate everything and ship it".

Most of the current visual assets started as images generated with ChatGPT. After that I manually cleaned them up, combined elements, adjusted composition, removed artifacts, changed colors, and generally processed them in Photopea until they worked reasonably well inside the game.

I treat these graphics more as a visual direction / prototype than a final locked art style.

The longer-term plan is actually to replace many of them with 3D scenes built in Godot and rendered back into 2D assets. I’m currently experimenting with recreating the game’s maps, terrain, cities and other elements in Godot, while keeping the existing 2D version of the game alive.

AI assistance on this project goes beyond graphics too. I've been using Codex mostly for:

* code reviews
* discussing architecture and possible approaches
* finding problems during larger refactors
* maintaining and updating project documentation
* learning

I still make the architectural and design decisions myself, but having something that can inspect a large codebase and challenge an implementation has been particularly useful for a solo project.

So the role of AI in the project keeps changing. At first it was mainly helping me create assets I simply couldn’t create myself. Now some of those assets are becoming references for a more traditional 3D pipeline.

So instead of:

**AI image → final game asset**

it is increasingly becoming:

**AI concept → manual editing → prototype → 3D recreation in Godot → rendered 2D asset**

comments.author: kilographix
comments.body: How much civ 3 influence is there

replies.author: ernestwisniewski
replies.body:
Quite a lot, actually. Probably a bit from every Civ game. I’ve taken inspiration from different parts of the series rather than trying to copy one specific entry.

Right now my main focus is on building stable foundations first. Once the core systems are solid, I want to add new mechanics gradually, one layer at a time, instead of throwing everything in at once and ending up with a chaotic mess.

The game is also being designed with 3–4 player multiplayer in mind, so I'm trying to keep the core systems predictable and manageable enough to work well in multiplayer too.
